lines.text: You awake slowly on a cold tile floor. The muffled wailing of alarms echo through your ears. Your vision slowly focuses and you glance around at your surroundings, desperately trying to understand where you are. But when you reach for your memories, there's just a void—an appalling nothingness.
Ugh, I should try and get out of here... Am i missing anything? (Press I to check your inventory)
Finally, I'm not sure if this is me, but it'll work, time to move on.
A Researcher ID. Is this me? The name field seems to have been charred off.
Level-2 keycard. Still strangely warm, like someone left in a hurry.
There's nothing else in here save for some pens and clips.
Nothing interesting is left in the locker.
Security door. I'll need a keycard to get through.
The badge reader demands a registered name before it will clear Me. I'll need to provide some form of identification first.
The reader chirps. The door unlatches into the east corridor.
Ugh... it's all so foggy. I can barely even remember my name...
(Something surfaced just now — a fragment of memory. They'll collect in your Memories. Press M to open them and start piecing together what happened.)
Rows of redacted entries. Someone circled a date—yesterday.
The clock above the door has stopped. 04:23... Just how long was I out for?
A biohazard container sits sealed and labeled. It seems to be empty, thankfully.
The substance in it looks viscous. Maybe it's gone bad.
Smaller bottles cluster together All labeled with substances that I can't recall the importance of.
A periodic table of elements hangs crooked on the wall. There seems to be 121 elements now.
This was a rubbish idea, why am I digging through trash?
Papers coat the floor like snow. You have the eerie feeling that you're being watched, hairs prickle upon the back of your neck.
Cafeteria memo: all break-room microwaves replaced. Mundane. Almost reassuring, there was human activity here recently.
You've already read this memo.
Incident follow-up—Subject interaction logged. Appendix pages torn out. [REDACTED] exhibited strange, familial traits towards the scientists today.
Beneath it lies a heavier sheet—form EH-14. The text is dense, but legible if you take the time to read it.
Scorch marks on the floor. Whatever was here left in a hurry.
Personnel roster. Every name blacked out except one—unreadable, but familiar.
There's nothing else interesting here.
The Research lab feels safer than the corridor.
Labs 12–21. The card reader is dark—whatever happened here, no one left this wing on schedule.
Labs 22–31. A faint chemical tang seeps under the door. Nothing good waits on the other side.
Another sealed lab door. The handle is warm, as if something pressed against it from within.
A wall-mounted directory sign. An arrow points left to LABS 28–31; right to LABS 32–35.
The numbers climb the deeper the Archives go. Whatever they kept down here, they didn't want it near the surface.
The rearmost door on the right wing shudders. Metal screeches. The lock disengages with a dull clunk and the sliding door swings inward—no one touched it.
Emergency light spills through the frame, painting the far wall in red.
You spin toward the opening, heart slamming against your ribs.
A middle-aged man in tactical gear staggers through the opening—rifle slung, uniform soaked with sweat, eyes wild and bloodshot.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: —the hell? You're not clearance staff. Who are you?
He looks as surprised as you feel. For a moment neither of you moves.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Why are you still here? The evacuation order started thirty minutes ago! We need to leave immediately.

choices.text: Tell the Truth: Tell him you woke up with no memory—that he's the first person you've seen.

reaction.headline: He believes you.
reaction.detail: His grip on the rifle eases. For the first time, he looks at you like a person—not a problem.

choices.text: Be Vague: I couldn't find my keycard. It had fallen under the equipment in the Lab. *You point towards the room you were just in.

reaction.headline: He doesn't buy it.
reaction.detail: His jaw tightens. Whatever patience he had is gone—replaced by the sharp edge of someone who has already seen too many bodies today.

lines.text: You don't know who this man is, but he's the first living person you've met since you awoke. The words spill out before you can second-guess them.
You tell him everything—waking on the floor, the blank where your memories should be, the alarms, the empty rooms.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: ...Amnesia? Christ. Okay. Okay—breathe. I believe you. You look scared out of your mind, and nobody in their right mind would play games right now.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Listen, something went wrong in the labs—breach protocols, containment failures. This whole wing is compromised. We cannot stay here.

choices.text: Nod and follow him.

reaction.headline: He's glad you came clean.
reaction.detail: He nods once—grateful, hurried—and starts moving like every second still matters.

lines.text: You keep your face flat and offer the only excuse you can think of.
I couldn't find my keycard. It had fallen under the equipment in the Lab.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Under the—are you kidding me? Evac doesn't wait while you tear apart a supply closet!

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: We had a containment breach. People are dead. You do not wander off for paperwork. You move when I say move.

choices.text: Stay quiet and follow.

reaction.headline: He's watching you.
reaction.detail: He doesn't argue further, but his eyes never quite leave you. Trust here is a luxury neither of you can afford.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: I'm Chase—facility security. Stick close, watch my back, and don't touch anything labeled with a hazard stripe.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: The forward door is still on emergency power. We go through there, get you to the checkpoint, figure out who you are.
He jerks his chin toward the open door behind him—the same one he just stumbled through.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: I'm Chase. Security. You will do exactly what I tell you, when I tell you—no detours, no questions in a hot zone.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Containment is blown. Air's wrong. If you lag behind, I leave you. That door stays open another minute—move.
He shoves past you toward the rearmost open doorway, rifle up, expecting something worse than you in the dark ahead.
(You follow Chase through the open door.)

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Keep with me. This is Research Wing C—we're clear of the Lab wing now, but we're not safe.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: The Archives isn't named because it's a sort of library. this is just the intake and documentation block for contained specimens—manifests, sealed records, everything the public never sees.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Command issued a facility-wide evacuation when the labs breached containment. Alarms, then radio silence. That order went out over thirty minutes ago.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Most research staff never reached the muster points. I was on a final sweep when the network died—and then I found you still inside.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: I don't know how you missed the first wave. Right now we reach the checkpoint, figure out who you are, and stay breathing.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Research Wing C. Eyes forward. We don't stop again until we're clear of this floor.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: The Archives catalog what this place actually holds. Specimens. Intake files. Everything they buried under classification.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Evacuation went facility-wide when containment failed in the labs. Thirty minutes ago. You should have been gone with the first wave—not digging through rooms.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Half the researchers in this building are dead or worse. I wasn't hired to babysit stragglers, but the sweep's done and you're here.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: You'll get answers at the checkpoint if we live that long. Move.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Catch your breath. We've got a few seconds before the next stretch—use them. Anything you need to ask, ask now.

choices.text: Why is the whole facility being evacuated?
What was I even doing here? Why was I in the research department?
How close are we to the exit?
No more questions. Let's continue.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Containment failed. A lot of the experiments down here broke loose, and the ones that did will kill you if you so much as share a corridor with them.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Command's solution is to seal the entire site as one unit—doors, levels, everything—and write it off.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: I was running the final sweep. Making sure the place was empty before they close the lid. That's when I found you.

choices.text: Why is the whole facility being evacuated?
What was I even doing here? Why was I in the research department?
How close are we to the exit?
No more questions. Let's continue.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Your work? Couldn't tell you. I run security, not the personnel roster.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: But you walked out of the Research wing with a researcher's ID, so that's what you are. A researcher.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Whatever you were assigned to, it was one of the more docile areas. If you'd been posted near the bad wings, we wouldn't be having this conversation.

choices.text: Why is the whole facility being evacuated?
What was I even doing here? Why was I in the research department?
How close are we to the exit?
No more questions. Let's continue.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: The exit? Further than I'd like.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: This place has more floors than even I've ever been cleared to see. I don't know where the bottom is, and I'd rather not find out.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: What I do know is that we're deep—down in the laboratory levels, at least. We climb from here. Slow, and quiet.

choices.text: Why is the whole facility being evacuated?
What was I even doing here? Why was I in the research department?
How close are we to the exit?
No more questions. Let's continue.

lines.text: You slip back into the littered east corridor. The open door and scattered papers are still there—Chase is ahead in Wing C if you need him.
Labs 12–21. The reader is dead; the door hasn't been opened since the alarms started.
More Labs. Something chemical burns your sinuses. You try the reader—dead. The door's locked tight.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Sealed from the inside when containment broke. That's not our way out—leave it.
A sealed lab door, scorched along the frame as if something tried to get out—or in. It won't budge.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Locked, and not the way we're going. Keep looking.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Hey—wrong way. That's back toward the block we just cleared. There's nothing behind us but locked labs and whatever's loose in them.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: We don't backtrack. We find the exit. Try the doors ahead.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: All of them sealed. Figures. The signage said the West Wing is this way—Labs 1 through 7.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: If there's a stairwell up and out of the Archives, it's through there. Stay close to me.
The corridor opens onto a wide doorway—standing open, darkness beyond. You're barely through when the frame screams and the door crashes down, sealing the gap.
Arcs of blue light crawl across its surface, snapping and humming. A Tesla gate—live.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: A containment gate. Nothing on the index gets past one of these alive... which means we're on the wrong side of it now. We can't go back.
Somewhere behind you, back from whence you came, something shifts—a slow, dragging scrape of weight across concrete, then a wet, clicking exhale.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: ...Quiet. Don't move.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: That's not the gate. Something's loose in here with us—wandering. And it just heard the door come down.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: Move. MOVE—back toward the stairs, now!
You turn. Something vast comes out of the dark between heartbeats—no shape your eyes will hold. Chase shoves you sideways and raises his Rifle.

lines.speaker: Chase
lines.text: GO! Don't look back—find the—
The shot cracks once. Then a wet, final sound, and Chase isn't there anymore. His pistol skitters across the floor to your feet. His dog tags land beside it.
There's no time for both. The dark is already shifting toward you. Your hand hovers over the floor—
You snatch up the pistol—still warm from his grip—and leave the tags glinting on the concrete. Then you run.
You close your fist around the tags and leave the pistol where it fell. It felt wrong to take the gun and leave the man. Then you run.
A door. No time to read the placard—just pick one and move.
The camera bank flickers between feeds. On one of them, something is moving through the corridor you just left—and it's coming this way. You map its path in your head.
The door back to the stairwell. You could run for it—but you already saw what's loose on the camera feeds.
Going back out there now is a terrible idea. The vent's the smarter play, if you can get it open in time.

choices.text: Leave through the door anyway.
Stay in the security room.

lines.text: You pull the door open. The stairwell is wrong—too quiet, then a wet scrape of something vast turning toward you.
You step back from the door. Whatever's hunting out there can wait—you've got work to do in here first.
A red fire bell on the wall. The pull station's plastic seal is still intact. Nobody pulled it before the evacuation.
The desk terminal still shows the Archives security login. No time to hack it—the wall monitors are what you need.
A notepad on the desk, pencil stub beside it. Most pages are facility codes; the top sheet just says: log off after shift.
The drawer slides open on loose rounds rolling in the tray. You sweep them into your pocket. The pistol feels a fraction less useless.
Just an empty drawer and a few spent casings now.
A walkie-talkie, still warm with static. Someone, somewhere on another floor, might still be breathing.
Just static now.
A flat-head screwdriver from the desk drawer. Exactly what you'd need on a vent grille.
You've already taken the screwdriver.
A wall vent, the grille screwed shut. You'd need a screwdriver to get it open.
A wall vent at floor level, grille screwed in tight. The duct behind it runs off into the dark—away from the door, away from whatever's out there.

choices.text: I could use the screwdriver.
Leave it alone.

lines.text: You wedge the flat-head under the first screw and start working the grille loose.
You leave the grille where it is. The vent will still be here if you change your mind.
The screws give one by one and the grille drops away, clattering onto the floor. Where it was, a black duct gapes open in the wall—just big enough to crawl into.
(Click the opening to climb inside.)
Shelves of dead supplies and dust. For the first time in a while, the dark in here is just dark.
You drop out of the vent onto cold concrete and lie still, lungs burning. No dragging. No clicking. Just your own heartbeat.
A storage room. Sealed on one side. Safe—for now. You let yourself breathe, and Chase's tags bite into your closed fist.
The vent grille rattles with stale air. No movement inside—just the distant hum of failing climate control.
Directional signage: an arrow left for the WEST WING, another ahead for LABS 1–7. Someone's scratched EVAC across it in red paint.
A dome camera hangs overhead. Its status LED blinks amber—recording, or trying to.
(Reserved for a later encounter—after the Chase sequence.)
(Reserved.)
(Reserved.)
